fixes.explanation: A wall is protection, but that's not what God says here. He says their silver and gold "…cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD." It's not a wall around anybody. It "…became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity."

Ways is the one. God says, "I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations." He's looking at how they lived, plain and simple. The answer was right there in the verse, baker.
Neighbors is a fair guess, but God doesn't point to the folks next door. He says, "I will judge you according to your ways…" Their own ways are the measure. It's about how they lived.
Silence is a quiet guess, but that's not the word God uses. He says there is "…panic on the mountains instead of shouts of joy." Panic is what takes the place of the joy. Silence isn't in the verse.
Right on target. God says, "Their violence has grown into a rod to punish their wickedness." The rod grew out of their own violence. I think that's a heavy line, so it's worth hearing slowly.

Wrath is the word. God says, "Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon the whole multitude." The buyer and the seller are both told what not to do, and the reason is the same for both. Wrath is upon the whole multitude.
Not this time, friend. God says the vision concerning the whole multitude "…will not be revoked…" So He says it won't be taken back. It's a firm line.

That's the one. God says their silver and gold "…cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD." Instead, it "…became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity." So the wealth they trusted tripped them up.
God doesn't say neighbors, friend. He says, "…I will bring the most wicked of nations to take possession of their houses." Those who take the houses come from the nations, not from next door.
False is right. God says "…instruction from the priests will perish, as will counsel from the elders." So counsel from the elders won't be there for them. That's a lot of guidance gone.
